name: Ginger Tulsi Honey Decoction

ingredients.name: Raw Pure Honey
ingredients.notes: Natural demulcent to soothe irritated throat lining

preparation_steps: Bring 1.5 cups of water to a boil in a small pot.
Add the crushed ginger and washed Tulsi leaves into the boiling water.
Simmer on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until the liquid reduces to approximately 1 cup.
Strain the decoction into a mug and let it cool down to warm (not hot) temperature.
Stir in 1 tablespoon of raw honey thoroughly. (Do not add honey to boiling water as it degrades nutrients).
dosage_and_frequency: Sip 1 cup warm, 2 to 3 times daily, preferably once after waking up and once 30 minutes before bedtime. Continue for 3-5 days.
precautions_and_contraindications: CRITICAL: Do NOT administer honey to infants under 12 months (1 year) of age due to high risk of fatal infant botulism.
Avoid large amounts of concentrated ginger if taking anticoagulant medications (blood thinners such as Warfarin or Aspirin) as ginger has mild blood-thinning effects.
Do not consume on an empty stomach if you suffer from acute gastric hyperacidity or ulcers.
Diabetic patients should monitor blood glucose levels or substitute honey with warm water and pinch of cinnamon.
who_should_avoid: Infants under 12 months (due to Honey / Botulism hazard)
Patients scheduled for surgery within 2 weeks (due to ginger blood-thinning)
Patients on high-dose prescription blood thinners without doctor advice
Individuals with acute peptic or duodenal ulcers
possible_side_effects: Mild heartburn or throat warmth if ginger concentration is too strong

name: Turmeric Golden Milk (Haldi Doodh)

ingredients.name: Pure Turmeric Powder (Curcuma longa)
ingredients.notes: Rich in curcumin; potent natural anti-inflammatory

ingredients.name: Black Pepper Powder (Freshly ground)
ingredients.notes: Contains piperine, which boosts curcumin absorption by up to 2000%

ingredients.name: Milk (Cow milk, Almond milk, or Oat milk)
ingredients.notes: Fat content aids fat-soluble curcumin absorption

preparation_steps: Pour 1 cup of milk into a saucepan and place over medium heat.
Add 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder and a pinch of black pepper.
Whisk well and bring to a gentle simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and pour into a glass.
Allow to cool slightly before adding honey or jaggery to taste.
dosage_and_frequency: Drink 1 warm cup once daily at bedtime for 1-2 weeks.
precautions_and_contraindications: Avoid large doses of medicinal turmeric if suffering from gallstones, bile duct obstruction, or gallbladder diseases (turmeric stimulates gallbladder contractions).
Turmeric can slow blood clotting; stop taking at least 2 weeks before scheduled surgeries.
Do not exceed recommended turmeric dosage to prevent stomach upset or nausea.
Lactose intolerant individuals MUST use plant-based milk (almond, soy, oat).
who_should_avoid: Individuals with gallstones or biliary tract blockage
Patients taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications in high doses
Pregnant women in early stages should avoid high medicinal turmeric doses (dietary amounts are safe)
People with severe iron deficiency (excessive turmeric can bind with iron)
possible_side_effects: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort or yellowing of stools

name: Peppermint and Fennel Soothing Tea

ingredients.name: Dried Peppermint Leaves
ingredients.notes: Contains menthol which relaxes gastrointestinal smooth muscles

ingredients.name: Fennel Seeds (Crushed)
ingredients.notes: Carminative properties to expel gas and relieve spasms

preparation_steps: Lightly crush 1 teaspoon of fennel seeds using a mortar and pestle.
Place crushed fennel seeds and peppermint leaves into a tea infuser or mug.
Pour 1 cup of freshly boiled water over the herbs.
Cover with a lid and steep for 8-10 minutes to trap volatile medicinal oils.
dosage_and_frequency: Drink 1 cup warm 20-30 minutes after heavy meals or at the onset of bloating, up to 2 times daily.
precautions_and_contraindications: Individuals suffering from Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) or hiatal hernia should AVOID peppermint, as it relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter and worsens acid reflux.
Avoid excessive fennel tea during pregnancy as fennel in large doses possesses mild uterine-stimulating phytoestrogens.
Not suitable for infants under 2 years of age.
who_should_avoid: Severe GERD or severe acid reflux sufferers (peppermint aggravates acid regurgitation)
Pregnant women (fennel in concentrated medicinal amounts)
People allergic to plants in the Apiaceae (carrot/celery) family
possible_side_effects: Transient acid heartburn in susceptible individuals

name: Chamomile Lavender Relaxing Infusion

ingredients.name: Dried German Chamomile Flowers
ingredients.notes: Contains apigenin, an antioxidant that binds to brain receptors promoting calmness

ingredients.name: Culinary Lavender Buds
ingredients.notes: Aromatic compounds that reduce autonomic nervous arousal

preparation_steps: Place chamomile flowers and lavender buds into a tea cup or teapot.
Pour freshly boiled water over the flowers.
Strain the liquid, inhale the soothing aroma, and sip slowly.
dosage_and_frequency: Drink 1 cup 30 to 45 minutes before going to bed.
precautions_and_contraindications: Do NOT combine with prescription sedatives, sleeping pills, or central nervous system depressants without medical supervision.
Individuals allergic to plants of the Asteraceae/Compositae family (ragweed, marigolds, daisies) may experience allergic reactions.
Do not consume immediately prior to driving or operating heavy machinery.
who_should_avoid: People with known Asteraceae / Ragweed family allergies
Patients taking prescribed benzodiazepines or barbiturates (risk of additive sedation)
Individuals with severe hormone-sensitive cancers should avoid large amounts of lavender
possible_side_effects: Drowsiness, mild dizziness if consumed during daytime
